chunks: Surely We have sent apostles before you, some of whose account We have related to you, and that of some We have not told you. But no apost was given a miracle unless God dispensed. But when the decree of God comes the sentence is passed with justice; and the lovers of vice and vanity will then come to grief.

key_terms.الْمُبْطِلُونَ: the false claimers/those who negate truth

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of prophets' miracles being by God's permission?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the distinction between mentioned and unmentioned prophets underscores the universality of divine guidance, while the phrase 'by God's permission' (bi-idhn Allah) highlights the ontological dependence of miracles on the Divine Will rather than inherent power. This verse serves as a theological foundation for the concept of *Bada'* and the eventual triumph of truth, reminding believers that the final judgment will expose the emptiness of those who rejected the messengers' authentic signs.
